worksheets.title: Worksheet 1 — Input, Output and Conditionals
worksheets.description: Covers reading from standard input, formatted output, and branching. Write each program so it reads exactly the input shown in the test cases and prints exactly the expected output.

questions.title: Sum of two integers
questions.description: Read two integers from standard input, separated by whitespace, and print their sum on a single line.
questions.referenceNotes: In C use scanf("%d %d", &a, &b). In Python, int(input()) reads one line at a time — input().split() may be easier here.

questions.title: Largest of three numbers
questions.description: Read three integers on one line and print the largest of them. If several are equal to the largest value, print that value once.
questions.referenceNotes: Nested if-else, or the ternary operator. Do not use a sorting library — the point is the branching logic.

questions.title: Even or odd
questions.description: Read a single integer n and print the word Even if it is divisible by 2, otherwise print Odd. Match the capitalisation exactly.
questions.referenceNotes: The modulo operator (%) gives the remainder of a division. Watch out: in C, -3 % 2 is -1, not 1.

questions.title: Explain your approach
questions.description: In a comment at the top of your program, explain in three or four sentences how you decided which control structure to use for question 2, and what would change if the input could contain more than three numbers. Then print your name on a single line.
questions.referenceNotes: This question is graded by your teacher's reading of it, not by a test case.

questions.title: Factorial
questions.description: Read a non-negative integer n (n ≤ 12) and print n! on a single line.
questions.referenceNotes: A simple for loop accumulating into a running product. 0! is 1.

questions.title: Reverse an array
questions.description: The first line of input is n, the number of elements. The second line contains n space-separated integers. Print the same integers in reverse order, space-separated, on one line.
questions.referenceNotes: Read n first, then loop n times. Print a single space between values and a newline at the end — no trailing space.
